body:
## Outcome

Release Confidence Protocol 0.5.0 with reliable evidence capture and recovery, shorter agent instructions, and a simpler regression suite.

A successful command can support a coding claim only when its recorded source is known and unchanged across execution and validation. The CLI now provides compact run receipts, atomic obligation recording, preserving initialization recovery, and clear source-scope output. It handles concurrent writers, unsafe evidence files, cancellation, and unavailable Git provenance explicitly.

The skill keeps proof/review/completion requirements while moving conditional detail into references. Test cleanup removes 171 net lines and eight unnecessary Git-repository setups while retaining all 179 core tests and their assertions. Optional typed capture failures and bounded-output features are deferred.

## Validation

- Approved candidate `5008377`: 179 tests pass on macOS Python 3.10/3.12/3.14; Linux passes 177 with two filesystem-case skips.
- Before/after suites detect five injected semantic faults; healthy and benign controls pass. Independent fixture/CLI review found no actionable issue.
- All 29 candidate patches replay to the exact expected tree.
- Release commit changes only manifest/runtime version metadata and changelog. Repository CI and a fresh local full suite validate the release head before merge.

## Compatibility and rollout

Old Git-diff bindings require recapture for current-code completion. `init` and `record` use Unix directory locking. Source proof covers Git-enumerated working-tree content, not ignored dependencies, external services, or transient change-and-revert. Start new Codex tasks after updating the plugin.

Retain the previous installation for rollback. This establishes scoped mechanics and regression evidence; team productivity and generated-code quality improvements remain pilot outcomes to measure.
title: Release Confidence Protocol 0.5: reliable evidence and simpler agent workflow
